audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Passover/Pesach, unleavened bread, firstborn judgment, mixed multitude, memorial, and liberation night.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses and Aaron in land of Egypt, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

verses.restored: This month shall be for you beginning of months; it shall be first for you of months of year.

familiar.text: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.

verses.restored: Speak to all congregation of Israel, saying: On tenth of this month each shall take for themselves a lamb by fathers' house, a lamb for household.

familiar.text: Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house:

verses.restored: If the household is too small for a lamb, then one and neighbor near one's house shall take according to number of souls/lives; according to each one's eating you shall count for the lamb.

familiar.text: And if the household be too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbour next unto his house take it according to the number of the souls; every man according to his eating shall make your count for the lamb.

verses.restored: Your lamb shall be complete, male, son of a year; from sheep or goats you may take it.

familiar.text: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats:

verses.restored: It shall be for you under guard until fourteenth day of this month, and all assembly of congregation of Israel shall slaughter it between the evenings.

familiar.text: And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.

verses.restored: They shall take from the blood/life and put on two doorposts and lintel upon houses in which they eat it.

familiar.text: And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.

verses.restored: They shall eat the flesh in that night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.

familiar.text: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs they shall eat it.

verses.restored: Do not eat from it raw or boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head with its legs and its inward parts.

familiar.text: Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.

verses.restored: You shall not leave from it until morning; what remains from it until morning you shall burn with fire.

familiar.text: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; and that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.

verses.restored: Thus you shall eat it: your hips girded, your sandals on your feet, your staff in your hand; you shall eat it in haste. It is Pesach/Passover to YHWH.

familiar.text: And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD’s passover.

verses.restored: I will pass through land of Egypt in this night and strike every firstborn in land of Egypt, from human to beast; and upon all gods of Egypt I will do judgments. I am YHWH.

familiar.text: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD.

verses.restored: The blood/life shall be for you a sign upon houses where you are; I will see the blood/life and pass over you, and plague shall not be upon you for destruction when I strike land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

verses.restored: This day shall be for you memorial, and you shall celebrate it as festival to YHWH; throughout your generations, as age-long statute you shall celebrate it.

familiar.text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

verses.restored: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. Surely on first day you shall remove leaven from your houses; for everyone eating leavened bread from first day until seventh day, that soul/life shall be cut off from Israel.

familiar.text: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

verses.restored: On first day there shall be holy calling/assembly, and on seventh day holy calling/assembly for you; no work shall be done in them, only what every soul/life eats, that alone may be done by you.

familiar.text: And in the first day there shall be an holy convocation, and in the seventh day there shall be an holy convocation to you; no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat, that only may be done of you.

verses.restored: You shall keep unleavened bread, because on this very day I brought your hosts out from land of Egypt; you shall keep this day throughout your generations as age-long statute.

familiar.text: And ye shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day in your generations by an ordinance for ever.

verses.restored: In first month, on fourteenth day of month in evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until twenty-first day of month in evening.

familiar.text: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.

verses.restored: Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses; for everyone eating what is leavened, that soul/life shall be cut off from congregation of Israel, among sojourner and native of land.

familiar.text: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.

verses.restored: You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.

familiar.text: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.

verses.restored: Moses called all elders of Israel and said to them, Draw out and take flock-animals for yourselves according to your clans, and slaughter the Pesach/Passover.

familiar.text: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover.

verses.restored: Take bundle of hyssop, dip in blood/life that is in basin, and touch lintel and two doorposts with blood/life in basin; none of you shall go out from opening of one's house until morning.

familiar.text: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning.

verses.restored: YHWH will pass through to strike Egypt; he will see blood/life on lintel and two doorposts, and YHWH will pass over opening and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.

familiar.text: For the LORD will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the LORD will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.

verses.restored: You shall keep this matter as statute for you and your children into the age.

familiar.text: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.

verses.restored: When you come to the land that YHWH will give you, as he spoke, you shall keep this service.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, when ye be come to the land which the LORD will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.

verses.restored: And when your children say to you, What is this service to you?

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?

verses.restored: you shall say, It is sacrifice of Pesach/Passover to YHWH, who passed over houses of children of Israel in Egypt when he struck Egypt and rescued our houses. The people bowed low and worshiped.

familiar.text: That ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of the LORD’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.

verses.restored: The children of Israel went and did; as YHWH commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel went away, and did as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

verses.restored: It happened at midnight: YHWH struck every firstborn in land of Egypt, from firstborn of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to firstborn of captive who was in house of pit, and every firstborn of beast.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

verses.restored: Pharaoh rose in the night, he and all his servants and all Egypt, and there was great cry in Egypt, for there was no house where there was not dead.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

verses.restored: He called Moses and Aaron by night and said, Rise, go out from midst of my people, both you and children of Israel; go serve/worship YHWH according to your word.

familiar.text: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as ye have said.

verses.restored: Also take your flock and herd, as you spoke, and go; and bless me also.

familiar.text: Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.

verses.restored: Egypt pressed upon the people, to hurry to send them from the land, for they said, All of us are dead ones.

familiar.text: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, that they might send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We be all dead men.

verses.restored: The people lifted their dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls bound in their garments upon their shoulders.

familiar.text: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

verses.restored: The children of Israel did according to word of Moses and asked from Egypt objects of silver, objects of gold, and garments.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment:

verses.restored: YHWH gave the people favor in eyes of Egypt, and they let them have what they asked; and they plundered Egypt.

familiar.text: And the LORD gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.

verses.restored: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand footmen, the men apart from little ones.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.

verses.restored: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, and flock and herd, very heavy livestock.

familiar.text: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.

verses.restored: They baked the dough they brought out from Egypt into unleavened cakes, for it was not leavened, because they were driven out from Egypt and could not delay, and also they had not made provisions for themselves.

familiar.text: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt, for it was not leavened; because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual.

verses.restored: The dwelling of children of Israel, which they dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred thirty years.

familiar.text: Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.

verses.restored: It happened at end of four hundred thirty years, on this very day, all hosts of YHWH went out from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.

verses.restored: It is night of keeping watch to YHWH for bringing them out from land of Egypt; this night belongs to YHWH, keeping watch by all children of Israel throughout generations.

familiar.text: It is a night to be much observed unto the LORD for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of the LORD to be observed of all the children of Israel in their generations.

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses and Aaron, This is statute of Pesach/Passover: no foreign son shall eat of it.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: There shall no stranger eat thereof:

verses.restored: But every servant bought with silver, when you circumcise him, then he may eat of it.

familiar.text: But every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.

verses.restored: A settler and hired worker shall not eat of it.

familiar.text: A foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof.

verses.restored: In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not bring out from house any of flesh outside, and bone you shall not break in it.

familiar.text: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.

verses.restored: All congregation of Israel shall do it.

familiar.text: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

verses.restored: When a sojourner sojourns with you and would make Pesach/Passover to YHWH, let every male of his be circumcised; then he may come near to do it, and he shall be like native of land. But no uncircumcised one shall eat of it.

familiar.text: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.

verses.restored: One instruction/Torah shall be for native and for sojourner sojourning in your midst.

familiar.text: One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.

verses.restored: All children of Israel did as YHWH commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.

familiar.text: Thus did all the children of Israel; as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.

verses.restored: It happened on this very day: YHWH brought children of Israel out from land of Egypt according to their hosts.

familiar.text: And it came to pass the selfsame day, that the LORD did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

translation_notes: Pesach/Passover is preserved with Hebrew term and explained through passing-over/protection and liberation night.
The calendar is reoriented around liberation; time begins again for the freed people.
Mixed multitude in v.38 is crucial: liberation includes non-Israelites joining the exodus.
One Torah/instruction for native and sojourner in v.49 should be preserved as covenant inclusion with boundary markers.
Plunder language represents transfer from oppressor wealth after forced labor; avoid glamorizing theft detached from oppression context.
safety_note: This chapter contains the death of firstborn and must be handled with solemnity. Keep it tethered to Pharaoh's death-policy, repeated hardening, and liberation from systemic oppression. Do not generalize into violence theology or anti-Egyptian hatred.
